column1: The Happiness Industry: How the Government and Big Business Sold Us Well-Being
column2: 《幸福产业：政府和大企业如何向我们兜售幸福》

column1: By William Davies
column2: 威廉·戴维斯 著
column3: By William Davies|威廉·戴维斯著

column1: ‘Happiness is the ultimate goal because it is self-evidently good.
column2: “幸福是终极目标，因为幸福本身是好的，这一点不言自明。

column1: If we are asked why happiness matters we can give no further external reason.
column2: 如果有人问幸福为什么重要，我们说不出什么进一步的外在理由。

column1: It just obviously does matter.’
column2: 它显然就是重要的。”

column1: This pronouncement by Richard Layard, an economist and advocate of ‘positive psychology’, summarises the beliefs of many people today.
column2: 这番断言出自经济学家、“积极心理学”的倡导者理查德·莱亚德之口，概括了当今许多人的信念。

column1: For Layard and others like him, it is obvious that the purpose of government is to promote a state of collective well-being.
column2: 在莱亚德及其同道看来，政府的宗旨显然是增进全社会的福祉。

column1: The only question is how to achieve it, and here positive psychology — a supposed science that not only identifies what makes people happy but also allows their happiness to be measured — can show the way.
column2: 唯一的问题是如何实现这一目标。在这方面，积极心理学——这门据称既能找出什么能让人快乐、又能测量幸福程度的科学——可以指明方向。

column1: Equipped with this science, they say, governments can secure happiness in society in a way they never could in the past.
column2: 他们说，有这门科学在手，政府就能够以前所未有的方式确保社会幸福。

column1: It is an astonishingly crude and simple-minded way of thinking, and for that very reason increasingly popular.
column2: 这种思考方式粗糙、浅陋得令人吃惊，偏偏也正因为如此而越来越受欢迎。
column6: for that very reason|恰恰出于这个原因

column1: Those who think in this way are oblivious to the vast philosophical literature in which the meaning and value of happiness have been explored and questioned, and write as if nothing of any importance had been thought on the subject until it came to their attention.
column2: 持这种见解的人对浩如烟海的哲学文献浑然不知，而这些文献早已探讨并质疑过幸福的意义和价值。他们写起文章来，仿佛在他们留意到这个问题之前，就从未有人对此提出过任何重要的见解。
column8: of any importance|有任何重要意义
column9: came to their attention|引起他们注意

column1: It was the philosopher Jeremy Bentham (1748—1832) who was more than anyone else responsible for the development of this way of thinking.
column2: 对这种思考方式的形成影响最大的人，是哲学家杰里米·边沁（1748—1832）。
column4: more than anyone else|比其他任何人都更

column1: For Bentham it was obvious that the human good consists of pleasure and the absence of pain.
column2: 在边沁看来，对人而言，善显然就在于享有快乐、免受痛苦。
column3: the human good|对人而言的善

column1: The Greek philosopher Aristotle may have identified happiness with self-realisation in the 4th century BC, and thinkers throughout the ages may have struggled to reconcile the pursuit of happiness with other human values, but for Bentham all this was mere metaphysics or fiction.
column2: 公元前4世纪，希腊哲学家亚里士多德或许曾将幸福等同于自我实现，历代思想家也许曾苦苦思索，如何调和对幸福的追求与其他人类价值；但对边沁来说，这一切都只是形而上学或虚构罢了。
column3: identified happiness with|把幸福等同于
column7: pursuit of happiness|对幸福的追求

column1: Without knowing anything much of him or the school of moral theory he established — since they are by education and intellectual conviction illiterate in the history of ideas — our advocates of positive psychology follow in his tracks in rejecting as outmoded and irrelevant pretty much the entirety of ethical reflection on human happiness to date.
column2: 我们这些积极心理学的倡导者对边沁本人和他创立的道德理论学派所知甚少，原因在于他们所受的教育和所持的学术信念，使他们几乎不懂思想史。可是他们仍沿着边沁的足迹，把迄今关于人类幸福的伦理思考几乎全盘斥为过时且无关紧要。
column3: school of moral theory|道德理论学派
column7: follow in his tracks|循着他的足迹

column1: But as William Davies notes in his recent book The Happiness Industry, the view that happiness is the only self-evident good is actually a way of limiting moral inquiry.
column2: 但正如威廉·戴维斯在新作《幸福产业》中指出的那样，把幸福视为唯一不证自明的善，实际上是在限制道德探究的范围。
column4: the only self-evident good|唯一不证自明的善

column1: One of the virtues of this rich, lucid and arresting book is that it places the current cult of happiness in a well-defined historical framework.
column2: 这本书内容丰富、条理清楚、引人深思。它的一项长处，是将当下对幸福的狂热崇拜置于一个界定清晰的历史框架中。
column6: cult of happiness|对幸福的狂热崇拜

column1: Rightly, Davies begins his story with Bentham, noting that he was far more than a philosopher.
column2: 戴维斯从边沁讲起很有道理，因为他指出，边沁的身份远不止哲学家这一种。

column1: Davies writes, ‘Bentham’s activities were those which we might now associate with a public sector management consultant’.
column2: 戴维斯写道：“今天，我们或许会把边沁所做的种种事情同公共部门管理顾问的工作联系起来。”

column1: In the 1790s, he wrote to the Home Office suggesting that the departments of government be linked together through a set of ‘conversation tubes’, and to the Bank of England with a design for a printing device that could produce unforgeable banknotes.
column2: 18世纪90年代，他写信给英国内政部，建议用一套“传声筒”把各政府部门连接起来；还给英格兰银行寄去一份印刷设备设计方案，称这种设备能印出无法伪造的纸币。

column1: He drew up plans for a ‘frigidarium’ to keep provisions such as meat, fish, fruit and vegetables fresh.
column2: 他还拟订了一种“冷藏室”的设计方案，用来给肉、鱼、水果、蔬菜等食物保鲜。

column1: His celebrated design for a prison to be known as a ‘Panopticon’, in which prisoners would be kept in solitary confinement while being visible at all times to the guards, was very nearly adopted.
column2: 他设计了一种著名的监狱，被称为“全景敞视监狱”。在这里，囚犯各自被单独关押，却时时都在看守的视线之内。这项设计差一点就被采用。
column7: visible at all times|始终处于视线内
column8: very nearly adopted|差一点就被采用

column1: (Surprisingly, Davies does not discuss the fact that Bentham meant his Panopticon not just as a model prison but also as an instrument of control that could be applied to schools and factories.)
column2: （出人意料的是，戴维斯没有谈到一点：边沁设想的全景敞视监狱既是一种模范监狱，也是一种可以推广到学校和工厂的控制手段。）

column1: Bentham was also a pioneer of the ‘science of happiness’.
column2: 边沁也是“幸福科学”的先驱。

column1: If happiness is to be regarded as a science, it has to be measured, and Bentham suggested two ways in which this might be done.
column2: 要把幸福当作一门科学来研究，就必须对它加以测量。边沁提出了两种可能的测量方法。
column3: is to be regarded as|要被视为

column1: Viewing happiness as a complex of pleasurable sensations, he suggested that it might be quantified by measuring the human pulse rate.
column2: 他把幸福看作各种愉悦感觉的组合，因而提出也许可以通过测量人的脉率来量化幸福。

column1: Alternatively, money could be used as the standard for quantification: if two different goods have the same price, it can be claimed that they produce the same quantity of pleasure in the consumer.
column2: 另一种方法是拿金钱作为量化标准。如果两件不同的商品价格相同，就可以据此声称，它们给消费者带来的快乐也同样多。

column1: Bentham was more attracted by the latter measure.
column2: 后一种衡量办法更吸引边沁。

column1: By associating money so closely to inner experience, Davies writes, Bentham ‘set the stage for the entangling of psychological research and capitalism that would shape the business practices of the twentieth century’.
column2: 戴维斯写道，边沁把金钱和内心体验联系得如此紧密，从而“为心理学研究与资本主义日后交织在一起奠定了基础；这种交织将塑造20世纪的商业实践”。
column5: set the stage for|为……奠定基础

column1: The Happiness Industry describes how the project of a science of happiness has become integral to capitalism.
column2: 《幸福产业》描述了建立幸福科学的计划如何成为资本主义不可分割的一部分。
column4: a science of happiness|一门研究幸福的科学
column5: integral to|……不可分割的一部分

column1: We learn much that is interesting about how economic problems are being redefined and treated as psychological maladies.
column2: 经济问题如何被重新界定，并当作心理疾患来处置，书中就此讲述的许多内容都颇有意思。

column1: In addition, Davies shows how the belief that inner states of pleasure and displeasure can be objectively measured has informed management studies and advertising.
column2: 此外，戴维斯还说明了这样一种观念如何影响管理学和广告业：愉悦与不愉悦的内在感受都可以客观测量。
column4: pleasure and displeasure|愉悦与不愉悦

column1: The tendency of thinkers such as J B Watson, the founder of behaviourism*, was that human beings could be shaped, or manipulated, by policymakers and managers.
column2: 行为主义*创始人约翰·华生等思想家倾向于认为，决策者和管理者可以塑造、甚至操纵人。

column1: Watson had no factual basis for his view of human action.
column2: 华生对人类行为的这种看法没有事实依据。

column1: When he became president of the American Psychological Association in 1915, he ‘had never even studied a single human being’: his research had been confined to experiments on white rats.
column2: 1915年他就任美国心理学会主席时，“甚至连一个人都没有研究过”：他的研究仅限于对白鼠做实验。
column4: American Psychological Association|美国心理学会
column5: a single human being|哪怕一个人
column6: had been confined to|一直局限于

column1: Yet Watson’s reductive model is now widely applied, with ‘behaviour change’ becoming the goal of governments: in Britain, a ‘Behaviour Insights Team’ has been established by the government to study how people can be encouraged, at minimum cost to the public purse, to live in what are considered to be socially desirable ways.
column2: 然而，华生把复杂事物简单化的模型如今得到广泛应用，“行为改变”成了政府的目标。在英国，政府成立了“行为洞察小组”，研究如何以最小的公共财政开支，引导人们按被认为有益于社会的方式生活。
column3: reductive model|把复杂事物简单化的模型
column6: Behaviour Insights Team|行为洞察小组

column1: Modern industrial societies appear to need the possibility of ever-increasing happiness to motivate them in their labours.
column2: 现代工业社会似乎需要用幸福有望不断增长的前景来激励人们劳作。

column1: But whatever its intellectual pedigree, the idea that governments should be responsible for promoting happiness is always a threat to human freedom.
column2: 但无论这种想法有怎样的思想渊源，认为政府应负责增进幸福，始终都会威胁人的自由。
